solutions.check: 32 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 31 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Boring thing, getting in food. in Devon

definitions.note: the definition stands for a noun: a town found in Devon

indicators.note: one piece gets inside the other, so the tool is put within the dish

parts.note: a dish is an item of food
an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A drill bit has somehow ended up in someone's dinner on a Devon holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; DAWLISH is a seaside town on its coast. The full stop after 'food' is a print blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawlish is a resort town on the south Devon coast, so it is a place found in that county.

clue.text: Servant came up with neat sort of fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a maid is a servant

indicators.note: a sort of something is a rearranged version, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A servant arrived with a tidy kind of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came up' turns MAID into DIAM; 'sort of' rearranges NEAT into ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is a fabric decorated with glittering artificial gems or sequins.

clue.text: One doesn't wade' through milk and honey here in Ireland?

definitions.text: One doesn't wade' through milk and honey here in Ireland?

parts.words: One doesn't wade' through milk and honey here in Ireland
parts.note: a land of milk and honey would have fords of milk, but this Irish place's name promises a ford of plain water

explanation.surface: Ireland is not quite the promised land flowing with milk and honey.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the Irish county's name as WATER FORD: the crossing you wade there is water, not the milk and honey of the biblical promised land.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is a city and county in the south-east of Ireland.

clue.text: Feeble, but not 'yet retired from office

definitions.meaning: weak, especially through age or illness
still working at the company, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone is frail but still holds down their job.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN FIRM, still employed by the business.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means physically weak, and read as two words it means still employed by a company.

clue.text: Writer makes cut

definitions.meaning: a journalist, especially one producing dull work to order

explanation.surface: An author decides to edit something out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a jobbing journalist, and to hack is to chop roughly.

clue.text: Rope needs a brush ?

definitions.meaning: a mooring line at a boat's bow is called by this name
the definition stands for a person: one whose work needs a brush

explanation.surface: Someone wants a rope and a brush for a job round the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is both the line used to tie up a small boat and an artist or decorator who works with brushes.

clue.text: Banter a prig feels to be out of place

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been moved, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-righteous person feels teasing is inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be out of place' rearranges the ten letters of A PRIG FEELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, frivolous teasing talk, much like banter.

clue.text: First place for furniture?

parts.note: leading the way, and also where household goods travel when you move house

explanation.surface: A question about where furniture should be put first.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means at the front, leading; it also names where furniture goes on moving day, a removal van.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the van is to be in the vanguard, at the front, and removal vans carry furniture.

clue.text: Composer famous for his last word

definitions.text: Composer famous for his last word

parts.words: Composer famous for his last word
parts.note: an Italian song composer whose best-known song is a farewell

explanation.surface: A composer remembered for something he said as he died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last word' suggests dying words, but Paolo Tosti's famous song is 'Good-bye!', a parting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Paolo Tosti was an Italian composer of songs, best known for the ballad 'Good-bye!'.

clue.text: That dope working on the sails ?

definitions.meaning: a sailor who shortens sail by tying in part of it

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a fool is busy rigging a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a joint of cannabis, and also one who reefs, tucking in part of a sail.

clue.text: " The great — Made my mate " (Stevenson)

parts.note: a line from Robert Louis Stevenson's poem to his wife, with the creator of his wife missing

explanation.surface: A quotation from Stevenson with a word left for the solver to fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Stevenson's 'My Wife', which ends 'The great artificer / Made my mate'; the gap is God as the skilled craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman or maker, here the divine creator who fashioned the poet's wife.

clue.text: Have a little sense!

definitions.meaning: to try a small amount of food or drink
one of the five senses, alongside smell and touch

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea for someone to show some common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to try a small amount of it, and taste is also one of the five bodily senses.

clue.text: Earliest goddess ?

parts.note: the goddess who arrives earliest each day is the Roman deity of the dawn

explanation.surface: A question about which goddess came first in mythology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earliest' suggests the oldest goddess in the pantheon, but it means the goddess of the earliest hour, the dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the Roman goddess of the dawn, the first light of the morning.

clue.text: Subsidiary activity over which we might be faulted

definitions.meaning: a second job or interest kept up alongside one's main work

definitions.text: over which we might be faulted
definitions.meaning: in tennis, a server who steps over the court's edge marking commits a foot fault

explanation.surface: A hobby that might get us criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is a secondary occupation, and also the boundary marking at the side of a court or pitch, which a player can be penalised for crossing.

clue.text: Gargantuan achievement

parts.note: Rabelais's giant Gargantua's offspring, his son, here thought of as what he produced

explanation.surface: A feat of enormous scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gargantuan' looks like a word meaning huge, but it means belonging to Gargantua, Rabelais's giant, whose achievement is his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantagruel is the giant son of Gargantua in the comic novels of Rabelais.

clue.text: Second person in the boathouse ?

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the letters of the word boathouse

explanation.surface: A question about who else is in the boathouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the old singular pronoun of the second person, the familiar form of 'you'.

clue.text: Made things easier when a friend returned the item

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: the word for an item is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: a detail is a single item or particular

explanation.surface: Things got easier once a friend gave back the borrowed article.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease or relieve, as palliative care eases symptoms without curing.

clue.text: Advisable to do shift work sometimes

definitions.meaning: suitable or wise in the circumstances
a shift is a makeshift device, something used to get a job done

explanation.surface: It can be wise to take night duties now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means advisable or convenient, and as a noun it is a shift or contrivance used to achieve a purpose.

clue.text: Tools bound to be found in uncle's place

parts.note: pawns are people used as tools by others
to bound is to hop or leap

explanation.surface: Tools tied up in a relative's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, so his place is where goods are pawned.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker's premises, where goods are left as security for a loan; 'uncle' is old slang for the pawnbroker.

clue.text: Perhaps he supplied material for "What's My Line?"

definitions.text: Perhaps he supplied material for "What's My Line?"

parts.words: Perhaps he supplied material for "What's My Line?"
parts.note: the old TV panel show's title read as an actor asking for a forgotten line

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote the old TV panel game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's My Line?' was a TV panel game about guessing jobs, but here it is an actor who has forgotten the words and needs them fed from the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompter is the person in a theatre who reminds actors of forgotten lines.

clue.text: Benefit obtained by good service, perhaps ?

definitions.meaning: in tennis, the point after deuce, which a strong serve can win

explanation.surface: A reward earned by working well for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a benefit, and in tennis it is the score after deuce that a winning serve can bring.

clue.text: Box in the yard ?

definitions.meaning: a yard on a sailing ship is a horizontal pole holding a sail

explanation.surface: A box left lying in someone's yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box in practice, and a ship's yard is a type of spar, a strong pole for rigging.

clue.text: Stays in bed as I might do!

indicators.note: do in its sense of to fix or arrange, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone lingers in bed, as the speaker would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might do' rearranges the letters of BED AS I.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or stay, so abides means stays.

clue.text: In short, boys need a protector

parts.note: Pat is short for Patrick, a boy's name
Ron is short for Ronald, another boy's name

explanation.surface: Briefly put, young lads need someone to look after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' says the two boys' names are clipped forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a supporter or protector, as a patron saint protects.

clue.text: Chaff appears hurtful to our seniors

parts.note: bad means harmful or hurtful
being 'in age' is being old, so the phrase reads as bad for those in their old age

explanation.surface: Teasing remarks are unkind to the older generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is light-hearted teasing, the same as banter or witty repartee.

clue.text: Lear character found by a gully

parts.note: Edward Lear's nonsense poem features the Dong with a Luminous Nose

explanation.surface: A character from King Lear turns up beside a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's king, but it is Edward Lear the nonsense poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A donga is a steep-sided gully or dry watercourse, a South African term.

clue.text: Daisy's mount

parts.note: the old song 'Daisy Bell' promises Daisy a ride on a bicycle built for two

explanation.surface: A question about the horse that someone called Daisy rides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests a horse, but Daisy of the music-hall song 'Daisy, Daisy' rides 'a bicycle made for two'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is a bicycle with seats for two riders, the machine in the song.

clue.text: But he hadn't a mother

parts.note: the first man in Genesis was made from dust, so had no parent who bore him

explanation.surface: An objection that someone was motherless.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'But' answers 'every man has a mother': the first man in the Bible was made from dust, not born.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam, the first man in the Bible, was created by God rather than born of a woman.

clue.text: Girl worker returns about one

indicators.note: the reversed word for a worker goes round, about, the letter for one
the word for a worker is read backwards, as if coming back

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A young woman comes back to work at about one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns HAND into DNAH, and 'about' puts it round I, giving D-I-NAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinah is a female first name, so it fits as a girl.

clue.text: Endured reading foreign articles — Newt Metamorphosis

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is the German definite article

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a change of form, so the letters of the word are changed round

explanation.surface: Someone suffered through reading a foreign-language book on how a newt transforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newt' looks like part of a book title, but it is fodder; 'reading' is a link. The articles are French and German, one from each language.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or suffer it, so underwent means endured.

clue.text: A hairy thing, the Spanish knife!

parts.note: the scalp is the skin of the head where hair grows
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a hairy Spanish blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small sharp blade used by surgeons.

clue.text: Vessel designed to check the waves ?

definitions.text: Vessel designed to check the waves ?

parts.words: Vessel designed to check the waves
parts.note: a type of low armoured warship whose name also means to keep a watch on something

explanation.surface: A ship built to calm the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check the waves' reads as calming the sea, but it is watching over them, and the name is also used for a radio monitor of airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor was a shallow-draught armoured warship, and to monitor is to keep watch on or check.
